newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks switch to losses at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks switch to losses at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks surrendered early gains and closed lower Tuesday on profit-taking, dealers said.

"The market rose steadily after the opening but then stalled when it topped its recent (five-year) highs, which is logical considering these days there's somewhat less volume," said Leopolo Olivari Sivori at traders Hector Bacque.
He predicted stocks would continue to regroup over the next few days and attempt a fresh rise next week.
The blue-chip MerVal index shed 0.4 percent to 849.02, slipping off a session high of 859.17.
It reached a five-year high of 856 three weeks ago, before devaluation fears in Brazil unleashed a sharp wave of selling.

"The bolsa's underlying tone is positive -- when prices drop, investors see it as a buying opportunity," said Gabriel Ruiz at brokers Tavelli. "This is linked to the fact that bond yields keep falling, which makes equities more attractive than fixed-income instruments."

The U.S. long bond yield skidded to a seven-month low of 6.38 percent Tuesday as the Treasuries market reacted positively to the second quarter Employment Cost Index and a budget deal in Washington, dealers said.
The bolsa's broad market index stayed in positive territory in the session, closing up 0.9 percent. Winners outpaced losers 36 to 24 and 28 issues closed flat.

Floor volume totaled 34.4 million pesos, higher than Monday's turnover of 30.6 million but weaker than recent tallies of 40 million, while over-the-counter deals shrank to 90.5 million pesos from 102.6 million Monday.
Best MerVal performers were cement stock Juan Minetti, steelmaker Siderar and Telefonica, which rose 2.2 percent, 1.9 percent and 1.8 percent, respectively.
